exact_title: The Effect of Amino Acids on Wound Healing: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis on Arginine and Glutamine
sections_or_headings: 1.2 Why It Is Important to Do This Review
3.4.3 Length of Hospital Stay and Patient Mortality

figures.title: Stages of skin wound healing
figures.summary: Hemostasis, inflammation, proliferation, and repair/remodeling over time; conceptual background.

figures.title: L-arginine metabolism and wound-healing metabolites
figures.summary: Arginase/iNOS pathways connect arginine to ornithine, proline, polyamines, and nitric oxide.

figures.title: Glutamine-to-arginine metabolism in human macrophages
figures.summary: Metabolic linkage among glutamine, ornithine, citrulline, arginine, and nitric oxide.

figures.title: Arginine study-selection flow diagram
figures.summary: 47 database + 8 other records; 39 after duplicates; 39 screened; figure reports 23 full texts; 5 studies included. Flow counts are not fully arithmetically reconcilable.

figures.title: Glutamine study-selection flow diagram
figures.summary: 95 database + 16 other records; 103 after duplicates; 103 screened; figure reports 69 full texts; 41 systematic-review studies and 39 meta-analysis studies. Exclusion arithmetic is not fully reconcilable.

figures.title: Risk of bias summary :  arginine
figures.summary: Generally low risk for sequence generation/allocation; less consistent blinding/other-bias domains.

figures.title: Risk of bias summary :  glutamine
figures.summary: Sequence generation low risk in all; several unclear/high ratings, especially other bias and selected blinding domains.

figures.title: Length of hospital stay forest plot :  glutamine
figures.summary: MD -2.65 days (95% CI -3.10 to -2.21), p<0.00001, I²=84%; 21 studies/1042 participants in prose.

figures.title: Lactulose/mannitol forest plot :  glutamine
figures.summary: MD -0.01 (95% CI -0.02 to -0.01), p<0.00001, I²=97%; 5 studies/210 participants.

figures.title: T-cell lymphocyte forest plot :  glutamine
figures.summary: SMD -0.16 (95% CI -0.33 to 0.01), p=0.07, I²=93%; forest plot totals 315 vs 312, conflicting with prose statement of 540 participants.

tables.title: Search terms and search strategy
tables.summary: PICO/search concepts for population, amino-acid intervention, outcomes, study designs, and Boolean combination.

tables.title: Arginine supplementation studies
tables.summary: Five included arginine studies with duration, population, n, dose, comparator, and reported wound-healing outcomes.

tables.title: Glutamine supplementation studies
tables.summary: Included glutamine trials with duration, populations, sample sizes, doses, control groups, and outcomes; table spans three pages.

source_integrity_issues.issue: Abstract hydroxyproline CI upper bound 4.45 conflicts with Results/Figure 8 upper bound 5.45.
source_integrity_issues.resolution: Preserve conflict; use Figure 8/Results value 5.45 for pooled-result atom and SEA quantitative synthesis because both agree.

source_integrity_issues.issue: Methods/Figures 9 and 15 identify standardized mean difference, but surrounding prose/abstract call the effect MD.
source_integrity_issues.resolution: Preserve conflict; use SMD when reporting forest-plot effect measure.

source_integrity_issues.issue: Figure 15 totals 315 experimental + 312 control (627) while Results prose says 540 participants.
source_integrity_issues.resolution: Preserve both; figure-derived denominator is used for the Figure 15 atom.

source_integrity_issues.issue: Abstract states ten electronic databases were used, while Methods explicitly names six search sources (including Google Scholar grey literature).
source_integrity_issues.resolution: Report both without inventing four unlisted databases.

source_integrity_issues.issue: Figures 4 and 5 contain selection counts that are not fully arithmetically reconcilable from the displayed nodes/categories.
source_integrity_issues.resolution: Represent displayed counts and flag the reconciliation problem.

omissions: Pure bibliography content is not condensed in SEA; all 115 references are preserved in the separate reference-processing queue.
